cases.title: Mega Sableye: build a three-slot plan, not a wall collection
cases.question: Which third member turns the Sableye / Galarian Slowking defensive cycle into progress against a particular opposing six?
cases.summary: Mega Sableye denies reflectable disruption and pressures physical attackers; Galarian Slowking resists Fairy and can pivot with Regenerator. That is a starting mechanism, not a universal matchup answer.

sets.name: Sableye
sets.spreads: Not optimized or recovered from the creator. Validation uses neutral nature, 32 HP / 2 SpD / 32 Speed points and 31 IVs solely as a legal smoke-test spread.

sets.name: Slowking-Galar
sets.spreads: Not optimized or recovered from the creator. Validation uses neutral nature, 32 HP / 2 SpD / 32 Speed points and 31 IVs solely as a legal smoke-test spread.

plans.title: Turn Fairy pressure into a recoverable pivot
prerequisites: A predicted Fairy attack rather than a coverage move
Slowking survives entry damage and the actual attack
A safe Chilly Reception or switch window exists
outcomes: Slowking takes half damage from Fairy typing before other modifiers
Regenerator restores health on switching out
Chilly Reception offers a slow pivot if the user survives to move
failureCases: Water coverage from Primarina is neutral rather than resisted
Ground, Ghost or Dark coverage threatens Slowking
Repeated entry damage or doubleswitches can exceed regeneration
Two defensive slots leave only one selected member to make progress

plans.title: Make physical setup expensive
prerequisites: Sableye can survive the incoming line
Opponent can be burned or its Attack makes Foul Play meaningful
Magic Bounce is active after Mega Evolution
outcomes: Reflect eligible status moves
Reduce damage from burn-sensitive physical attackers
Foul Play can exploit the target Attack stat
failureCases: Magic Bounce does not stop damaging Fairy moves
Fire types, Guts, Substitute or status immunity change the burn line
Gholdengo Good as Gold blocks many status approaches
Recovery can surrender tempo to a special attacker

plans.title: Select a third that forces progress
prerequisites: Name the opposing six and plausible sets
Choose which two of the defensive pair actually need to be brought
outcomes: Compare a Ground-immune pivot with an immediate breaker as alternative third slots
failureCases: Type coverage alone says nothing about breaking a recovery cycle
Two Mega candidates cannot both Mega Evolve in the same battle
Opponent changes the expected lineup

alternatives.helps: Can cover Ground attacks aimed at Slowking while resisting Fairy.
alternatives.cost: A third defensive member can make the selected three too passive; evaluate actual Body Press or other progress line.

alternatives.helps: Can threaten relevant Steel targets and provide a faster offensive route.
alternatives.cost: Adds Fairy and Ice vulnerabilities; no claim it is the best third.

alternatives.helps: A different damage profile instead of another defensive pivot.
alternatives.cost: Leaves Ground switching and speed decisions to the other slots.

warnings: Mega Sableye is neutral to Ghost and Dark, not resistant. It does not automatically cover those weaknesses for Slowking.
These two sets are new illustrative candidates, not extracted SplashPlate sets.
September Showdown usage is the latest inspected monthly snapshot, not a live October official ladder.
nextCalculations: Slowking switch-in survival against specified Primarina Water/Fairy variants at realistic HP
Third-slot candidate damage and recovery pressure against Gholdengo and opposing defensive cores
Bring-three selection against three explicit opposing sixes

hypotheses.claim: Retrieving condition-dependent switch and progress plans produces more useful third-slot suggestions than species-level type coverage.
hypotheses.test: Compare the same three suggested partners with exact threats, prerequisite chains and one exposed failure case each.

cases.title: Torterra / Mega Raichu Y / Milotic: protection and pressure
cases.question: Can Wide Guard and anti-Intimidate pressure give Mega Raichu Y enough safe turns without making Torterra passive?
cases.summary: Torterra supplies spread protection and targeted Ground/Grass damage. Mega Raichu Y supplies accurate attacks through its own No Guard. Competitive Milotic can punish opponent-induced stat drops. Their turn economy and switching rules determine whether the trio works.

sets.name: Torterra
sets.spreads: Not optimized or recovered from the creator. Validation uses neutral nature, 32 HP / 2 SpD / 32 Speed points and 31 IVs solely as a legal smoke-test spread.

sets.name: Raichu
sets.spreads: Not optimized or recovered from the creator. Validation uses neutral nature, 32 HP / 2 SpD / 32 Speed points and 31 IVs solely as a legal smoke-test spread.

sets.name: Milotic
sets.spreads: Not optimized or recovered from the creator. Validation uses neutral nature, 32 HP / 2 SpD / 32 Speed points and 31 IVs solely as a legal smoke-test spread.

plans.title: Buy Y-chu a turn against spread attacks
prerequisites: Opponent uses a blockable spread move
Torterra is free to use Wide Guard
Raichu has Mega Evolved and can act
outcomes: Wide Guard blocks applicable spread moves for the side
No Guard removes accuracy checks on attacks by or targeting Mega Raichu Y
Zap Cannon can apply damage and paralysis when the target is susceptible
failureCases: Single-target Earth Power or Ice Beam bypass Wide Guard
Opponent protects or switches to an Electric immunity
Raichu loses Lightning Rod when it Mega Evolves
No Guard also improves accuracy of incoming moves against Raichu

plans.title: Make opponent stat drops costly
prerequisites: Milotic is on the field when its own stats are lowered by an opponent
Opponent actually chooses or is forced into the stat-dropping action
outcomes: Competitive raises Milotic Special Attack by two stages when triggered
May discourage a stat-drop line that weakens physical Torterra
failureCases: Benched Milotic does not receive the trigger
Ally stat drops do not activate Competitive
Opponent can choose a different line
Milotic still needs attacks, speed and survivability to convert the boost

plans.title: Keep Ground pressure without damaging the ally
prerequisites: Choose a single-target Ground move or coordinate Protect/switch before Earthquake
outcomes: Headlong Rush damages the selected target without Earthquake friendly fire
failureCases: Headlong Rush lowers Torterra defenses
Earthquake hits grounded allied Raichu and Milotic
Protect consumes the ally attack opportunity
Rillaboom terrain can weaken Earthquake and alter targets

alternatives.helps: Armor Tail can block opposing priority directed at the side.
alternatives.cost: Grounded partner without Air Balloon is vulnerable to Earthquake; requires a slot and correct positioning.

alternatives.helps: Creates a different class of protected turn from Wide Guard.
alternatives.cost: Follow Me / Rage Powder differ; spread moves, powder immunity and redirect-bypassing abilities must be checked.

alternatives.helps: Hypnosis is an option to test with its own accuracy support.
alternatives.cost: Ally No Guard is not an accuracy aura; Milotic Hypnosis still checks accuracy unless user or target has relevant effects.

warnings: The linked prior team has base Raichu, not Mega Raichu Y, and a 0–3 result. It only establishes that this species trio has been used.
This is a role-oriented Torterra candidate, not the separate Shell Smash / Simple Beam composition.
No Guard does not bypass type immunity, Protect, or every form of prevention.
nextCalculations: Raichu survival against named single-target attacks that bypass Wide Guard
Torterra Headlong Rush and Wood Hammer damage against actual opposing sets
Compare using a guard turn versus attacking immediately
Assess Milotic Competitive-trigger opportunities against current Incineroar/Salamence usage without treating co-occurrence as wins

hypotheses.claim: A condition graph can discover role replacements by matching a protected-turn requirement instead of repeating one known combo.
hypotheses.test: Request alternatives to Wide Guard, then show exactly which attack classes each alternative permits or fails against.

cases.summary: Use a documented off-meta composition as an explainable plan graph, with distinct setup, protection, attack and fallback modes.

plans.title: Land Simple Beam before Shell Smash
prerequisites: Farfetchd moves before Torterra
Both survive to act
Simple Beam is not blocked or redirected
Torterra has an intact White Herb
outcomes: Simple doubles Shell Smash to +4 Attack, Special Attack and Speed and -2 defenses
White Herb clears negative stat stages when it activates
Inner Focus prevents flinch, including Fake Out flinch
failureCases: Inner Focus does not prevent Fake Out damage or a KO
Torterra loses Shell Armor when Simple overwrites its ability
White Herb can be consumed earlier
Choice Scarf locks Farfetchd into its selected move until switching
Torterra Protect blocks the ally Simple Beam
Opposing redirection can steal a redirectable ally-targeted move from a susceptible user

plans.title: Attack beside a Ground-immune partner
prerequisites: Active partner is immune to Ground in the actual state
Air Balloon remains intact or Levitate remains effective
outcomes: Torterra can use Earthquake without damaging that immune ally
failureCases: Air Balloon pops
Grounding or ability suppression removes immunity
Opponent Wide Guard blocks spread attacks
Ground-immune opponents require Rock Slide or a different attack

plans.title: Use another boost route
prerequisites: Alcremie can act and targets the intended ally
Choose whether Simple is already active
outcomes: Decorate can boost the ally through Protect
Simple can amplify eligible stat changes
failureCases: Aroma Veil is not general damage protection
Boosting still costs a support action
Status removal or opposing boost control can erase progress

plans.title: Choose a slower mode instead of blindly boosting Speed
prerequisites: Choose leads and backline for the actual opposing speed plan
Avoid treating +4 Speed and Trick Room as automatically complementary
outcomes: Trick Room offers a different turn-order mode
Simple plus Coil offers an Arbok boost route
failureCases: Speed boosting may be counterproductive in Trick Room
Opposing Taunt, damage or reversal can prevent the intended order
Selecting four members cannot preserve every six-member plan simultaneously

alternatives.helps: Ordinary Shell Smash needs one fewer enabler.
alternatives.cost: Smaller boosts; still needs a setup turn and survival.

alternatives.helps: Fake Out can buy a turn against an eligible target.
alternatives.cost: Only one target; Ghost immunity, priority blocking, terrain and opposing Protect alter the line.

alternatives.helps: Protect setup from a different class of attacks.
alternatives.cost: Does not replace Simple doubling, and not every attack redirects.
